answer: Random re-execution costs the network a fraction of duplicate compute, but it charges a sybil farm a full re-run for every identity it claims, since an unrelated peer repeats the work and compares output hashes. Because auditors rotate out of a shared pool and payment unlocks only after continuous uptime, a copied result is caught on the next audit and the identity loses its whole accrual instead of one reward, which turns a haven of clones into a tide that pulls out the moment a fresh cipher checks the work.
